title: Task contracts and policy engine
description: Fourteen task states, legal transitions, leases, audit journal and a deny-by-default policy engine, all property-tested.

title: Headless CLI
description: The vekrun CLI drives the same settings store and task lifecycle as the desktop app.

title: PTY sessions with output coalescing and backpressure
description: Rust-owned shells with coalesced output and pause/resume, measured against a raw transport.

title: Tabs, split panes and search
description: Tabs with shortcuts, draggable splits that never remount a shell, and scrollback search.

title: Session restore and shell integration
description: Layout and scrollback survive a restart under an honest divider. Exit codes, durations and failed-command markers come from shell integration marks.

title: SSH sessions
description: Remote shells with strict host-key checking, fingerprint acceptance and one-shot password prompts.

title: Windows shells verified by hand
description: PowerShell, cmd and WSL through ConPTY, exercised on a Windows machine rather than only in CI.

title: Credentials in the OS keychain
description: Secrets live in the keychain with a secret-free index; keys are deleted when a provider is removed.

title: Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and Gemini adapters
description: Streaming adapters in Rust, a capability registry that records unknowns, and a provider manager with a live connection test.

title: Ollama and LM Studio detection
description: Installed and reachable are reported separately. Model download guidance is not built yet.

title: Coding-agent account connections
description: Optional compatibility with existing coding-agent subscriptions through documented auth flows only.

title: Single-agent coding loop with approvals
description: Ask, Plan, Build, Debug and Review as policy profiles. Writes are shown as diffs for approval, with checkpoints and rollback.

title: Egress preview
description: What leaves the machine is shown before it leaves. The first contact with a hosted provider needs an explicit Send.

title: Scoped agent memory
description: User, project, team, agent, task and council scopes with enforced access, provenance and retention.

title: Git views through your installed git
description: Staging, diffs and commits run through the user's git so hooks and credential helpers apply.

title: Branches, worktrees and stashes in the Git view
description: Switch, create and delete branches, add and remove worktrees, stash and pop, all through your git and never forced. Destructive actions are confirmed and audited. Push, pull and fetch come with credentials in M10.

title: Built-in code editor
description: Monaco bundled locally, an explorer that respects ignore rules, search, saves that detect external edits instead of overwriting them, and a diff against HEAD. Language servers and diagnostics are not built.

title: Board with local tickets and Start Work
description: Tickets, repositories and Start Work into a worktree terminal, with an AI Agent mode and a Factory mode.

title: Linear, Jira, Asana, GitHub and GitLab ticket sources
description: Live providers behind one adapter interface with capability probes and status synchronisation.

title: Structured plans with approval
description: Plan mode produces a validated plan revision that is reviewed, approved and materialised into Factory tasks with traceability.

title: Council orchestration
description: An isolated first round, critique on positions only, moderator synthesis, evidence from tool ledgers, enforced limits, and your decision.

title: Manager and worker roles
description: Delegation under an authority that never widens, managers that wait for children, a concurrency cap and per-task worktrees.

title: Agent Inbox
description: One prioritised list of everything waiting for a person: approvals, escalations, decisions, reviews and blocked tasks.

title: Independent verification with bounded repairs
description: A different agent verifies with evidence. A pass without evidence is refused by the contract. Repairs are bounded and escalate.

title: Integrator with conflict preview
description: Merge preview with conflicts, approval before the merge, and a verified merge closing the chain.

title: Snapshots and restore
description: Uncommitted state is kept before risky turns and integration; restore is previewed, selective and undoable.

title: Durable background daemon
description: Tasks and the audit journal survive the window closing and a daemon restart without unsafe replay.

title: Remote workers
description: First-party Rust workers on a machine you control, over SSH port-forwarding by default, with reconnect and reconciliation.

title: Agent APIs
description: User-defined agent services with versioned, authenticated interfaces, bound privately by default.

title: Scheduling and standing orders
description: Cron-compatible schedules with time zones, event triggers and disclosed host requirements.

title: MCP client and server
description: Remote and local MCP servers through the policy engine, and a Vekrun MCP server that is off by default.

title: Extension host
description: Versioned manifests, declared capabilities and a sandboxed runtime for third-party extensions.

title: Signed installers for macOS, Windows and Linux
description: Public binaries appear on the download page only when they exist.
